title: Replying to @Lanie Jean TO CLARIFY: I realize of course that multiple...
transcript: Would a straight man ever play Mary in Oh Mary? And if so, who could do it justice? This question came up in the comments in my video about Oh Mary replacement casting. Someone pointed out that they're able to cast such a wide net because pretty much anyone can play this role. Someone else pointed out we haven't had a straight man play it yet. I wanna recognize, of course, there's a lot of complicated nuance here as far as gender, presentation and queer culture. All of that is extremely important and worth considering, but on an artistic level alone, I can't think of any straight men who could do it justice. Some of the suggestions in the comments here were Daniel Radcliffe, Andrew Garfield, and Channing Tatum. And look, I like these actors, but woof, I really hate the idea of them as Mary. I get it. Like, Daniel Radcliffe has been a very outspoken queer ally. Andrew Garfield, of course, has played a gay man on stage and won Tony for it. I just don't think it would be good. And I think it would so easily fall into that trap of just like, “oh, the joke is it's a straight man playing a woman.” “Ha ha ha!” If we were to get a straight man playing Mary, (and I'm not advocating for that, I think probably we'd be fine without it) But if we were, I think you would have to go with someone who has a lot of experience on the more like physical comedy / clown side of things. I'm thinking of someone like Bill Irwin or Mister Bean, where, like, what you lose from the sort of queer cultural understanding of camp, you make up for in, like, the technical expertise of physical and character comedy through clown work.
classificationReason: Reply-to-comments video ('Replying to @Lanie Jean') responding to viewer comments from a previous Oh Mary video about replacement casting. Primary purpose is responding to prior video's reaction, not reviewing the show.
